title: Florida Battles Record-Breaking Dengue Outbreak
subtitle: Health officials work to control the spread of the mosquito-borne virus as case numbers climb to historic highs.

summary.en: Florida is currently facing its largest dengue fever outbreak in decades, with over 250 locally acquired cases reported this year. Most of these infections are concentrated in Hillsborough County, near Tampa. Health officials have declared local emergencies and are working to reduce the mosquito population. While many people experience mild symptoms, the virus can cause severe pain and, in rare cases, death. Experts suggest that climate change may be helping these mosquitoes expand their reach into new areas.
summary.zh: 佛羅里達州目前正面臨數十年來最嚴重的登革熱疫情，今年已通報超過兩百五十例本土感染病例。這些感染多數集中在坦帕附近的希爾斯波羅郡。衛生官員已宣布進入地方緊急狀態，並致力於減少蚊蟲數量。雖然許多人僅出現輕微症狀，但該病毒可能導致劇烈疼痛，在罕見情況下甚至會致命。專家認為氣候變遷可能正協助這些蚊子將活動範圍擴展至新區域。

paragraphs.en: Florida is currently dealing with its most significant dengue fever outbreak in many decades. According to MedPage Today, state health officials have confirmed more than 250 locally acquired cases of the virus so far this year. This number is particularly concerning because it marks the highest count for any state in the continental United States since at least the 1940s. The vast majority of these infections have been reported in Hillsborough County, which includes the city of Tampa.
paragraphs.zh: 佛羅里達州目前正經歷數十年來最嚴重的登革熱疫情。根據醫學新聞網站「MedPage Today」報導，州衛生官員證實，今年以來該州已累計超過兩百五十例本土感染病例。此數據之所以令人擔憂，是因為這是自一九四零年代以來，美國本土各州中最高的紀錄。絕大多數的感染病例集中在包含坦帕市在內的希爾斯波羅郡。

paragraphs.en: This situation is an update to recent reports highlighting the growing health challenge in the region. While Puerto Rico often sees high numbers of dengue cases, the continental U.S. has typically seen much lower figures. However, Florida has now surpassed its previous record from 2023, when just under 200 locally spread cases were recorded. The current outbreak, which first became a major concern in July, is now close to exceeding the 264 cases reported in Hawaii during a 2015-2016 outbreak, which was previously the largest in a U.S. state in recent history.
paragraphs.zh: 此情況更新了近期關於該地區日益嚴峻的健康挑戰之報導。雖然波多黎各經常出現高數量的登革熱病例，但美國本土通常數據較低。然而，佛羅里達州目前的病例數已超越二零二三年不到兩百例的本土傳播紀錄。這波疫情自七月成為主要隱憂以來，目前已接近二零一五至二零一六年夏威夷州疫情期間所通報的兩百六十四例，該紀錄曾是美國各州近代史上最嚴重的疫情。

paragraphs.en: Dengue is a virus spread by a specific type of mosquito. Many people who catch it do not feel sick at all, but others develop fever, flu-like symptoms, and intense body aches. Because of this extreme pain, the illness is often called "breakbone fever." In very serious cases, the virus can lead to internal bleeding, shock, and even death. MedPage Today noted that there has already been one death in Florida this year linked to the virus: an elderly woman from Tampa who passed away on September 4.
paragraphs.zh: 登革熱是由特定蚊子傳播的病毒。許多感染者完全不會感到不適，但其他人則會出現發燒、類流感症狀以及劇烈的身體疼痛。由於這種極端的疼痛感，該疾病常被稱為「斷骨熱」。在極其嚴重的情況下，病毒可能導致內出血、休克甚至死亡。MedPage Today 指出，佛羅里達州今年已出現一例與該病毒相關的死亡案例：一名來自坦帕的年長女性於九月四日過世。

paragraphs.en: Local authorities are taking the situation very seriously. Officials in Hillsborough and nearby counties have declared local emergencies to help manage the crisis. In the Tampa area, workers are spraying for mosquitoes both day and night to reduce the number of insects that can carry the virus. Dawn Wesson, an expert on mosquito-borne diseases at Tulane University, explained that Florida often sees dengue because the state is a popular destination for travelers coming from places where the disease is already common, such as Puerto Rico.
paragraphs.zh: 地方當局正嚴肅看待此情況。希爾斯波羅郡及鄰近郡的官員已宣布進入地方緊急狀態，以協助控制危機。在坦帕地區，工作人員日夜進行噴灑作業，以減少攜帶病毒的蚊蟲數量。杜蘭大學（Tulane University）的蚊媒疾病專家韋森（Dawn Wesson）解釋，佛羅里達州常出現登革熱，是因為該州是來自波多黎各等疾病流行地區旅客的熱門目的地。

paragraphs.en: One of the biggest challenges in fighting dengue is the nature of the virus itself. There are four different types of the dengue virus. When a person is infected with one type, their body creates antibodies—proteins that help the immune system fight off germs—to protect them from that specific type for life. However, if that same person is later infected with a different type of the virus, these antibodies can sometimes fail to stop the infection. In some cases, they may even make it easier for the virus to enter the body’s cells and multiply. This complex behavior is a major reason why scientists have found it so difficult to create an effective vaccine, which is a medicine used to prevent a disease.
paragraphs.zh: 對抗登革熱最大的挑戰之一在於病毒本身的特性。登革熱病毒共有四種不同類型。當一個人感染其中一種時，身體會產生抗體（即協助免疫系統對抗病菌的蛋白質），以終身保護其免受該特定類型的侵害。然而，若該名患者隨後感染了另一種不同類型的病毒，這些抗體有時無法阻止感染。在某些情況下，它們甚至可能讓病毒更容易進入人體細胞並進行複製。這種複雜的行為是科學家難以研發出有效疫苗（用於預防疾病的藥物）的主要原因。

paragraphs.en: Experts are also looking at the bigger picture regarding how the disease spreads. While the mosquitoes that carry dengue have always lived in warmer parts of the U.S., their geographic range is growing. Scientists suggest that climate change is playing a role in this expansion, allowing these insects to survive in more areas than before. For many years, most dengue cases in the U.S. were only found in people who had recently traveled to other countries. The current situation in Florida shows that the virus is now finding ways to stay and spread locally.
paragraphs.zh: 專家們也正從更宏觀的角度審視該疾病的傳播方式。雖然攜帶登革熱的蚊子一直生活在美國較溫暖的地區，但牠們的地理分布範圍正在擴大。科學家認為氣候變遷在這種擴張中扮演了角色，使得這些昆蟲能在比以往更多的區域生存。多年來，美國大多數的登革熱病例僅見於近期曾前往其他國家的旅客。佛羅里達州目前的狀況顯示，該病毒現在正設法留存並進行本土傳播。

paragraphs.en: Globally, the situation is even more intense. According to the World Health Organization, there have been more than 2.2 million infections and nearly 1,200 deaths reported worldwide this year. Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shows that there have been nearly 1,900 locally acquired cases across the U.S. this year, with the majority occurring in Puerto Rico. As Florida continues its efforts to control the outbreak, health officials remain focused on public awareness and mosquito control to prevent the numbers from rising further.
paragraphs.zh: 在全球範圍內，情況甚至更為嚴峻。根據世界衛生組織（World Health Organization）統計，今年全球已通報超過兩百二十萬例感染，以及近一千兩百例死亡。美國疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）的數據顯示，今年全美已有近一千九百例本土感染病例，其中多數發生在波多黎各。隨著佛羅里達州持續努力控制疫情，衛生官員仍將重點放在提升公眾意識與蚊蟲防治，以防止病例數進一步攀升。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be greater than or to exceed a previous record or amount.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此字在新聞中常指打破紀錄，容易被誤認為單純的「經過」。文中：However, Florida has now surpassed its previous record from 2023, when just under 200 locally spread cases were recorded.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To use energy or substances to defend the body against an illness or infection.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語由動詞與副詞組成，意思與單純的「打架」不同，指身體防禦機制。文中：When a person is infected with one type, their body creates antibodies—proteins that help the immune system fight off germs—to protect them from that specific type for life.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The geographical area where a particular animal or plant species naturally lives.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「範圍」或「一系列」，這裡指生物分布的地理區域。文中：While the mosquitoes that carry dengue have always lived in warmer parts of the U.S., their geographic range is growing.

previousArticles.title: Florida Faces Its Largest Dengue Outbreak in Decades
previousArticles.summaryEn: Florida is currently experiencing its largest outbreak of dengue fever in many decades. Health officials have reported over 250 locally acquired cases, mostly in Hillsborough County. The virus is spread by mosquitoes, which are expanding their range due to warmer weather. While many people experience mild symptoms, the disease can cause severe pain and, in rare cases, death. Authorities are now taking emergency measures to reduce the mosquito population and protect the public.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason the current dengue outbreak in Florida is considered historically significant?

options.A: It has resulted in more deaths than any other virus in Florida history.
options.B: It is the highest count of locally acquired cases in the continental U.S. since the 1940s.
options.C: It marks the first time dengue has ever been detected in the Tampa area.
options.D: It has surpassed the total number of dengue cases recorded in Hawaii in 2015.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，佛羅里達州今年確認的本土感染病例數是自 1940 年代以來，美國本土各州中最高的。選項 A 錯誤，文中僅提到有一名長者死亡，並未說是史上最多死亡病例的病毒。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提及這是 Tampa 首次出現登革熱。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到目前的病例數正「接近」超過夏威夷 2015-2016 年的 264 例，尚未正式超越。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might the geographic expansion of mosquitoes be a concern for U.S. health officials?

options.A: Because mosquitoes are now carrying more types of viruses than they did in the past.
options.B: Because the climate is changing in a way that makes the virus immune to existing vaccines.
options.C: Because the virus is increasingly able to establish itself locally rather than relying on travel-related cases.
options.D: Because the mosquitoes are evolving to survive in colder climates where they were previously unable to live.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，過去美國多數病例源自國外旅遊，但佛州的現況顯示病毒已能「在地傳播」，這意味著病毒在美國本土落地生根的風險增加。選項 A 文中未提及蚊子攜帶的病毒種類變多。選項 B 錯誤，文中提到疫苗研發困難是因為病毒本身的複雜性，而非氣候變遷。選項 D 雖然提到氣候變遷讓蚊子分布擴大，但文中並未明確指出蚊子已能適應「寒冷」氣候，僅提到溫暖區域的擴張。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'antibodies' refer to in the context of the immune system's response?

options.A: Proteins that identify and neutralize foreign pathogens like viruses.
options.B: The cells that carry the dengue virus throughout the human body.
options.C: A type of medicine used to prevent the development of a disease.
options.D: The physical pain caused by the virus entering the body's cells.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文章第五段明確定義 antibodies 為「proteins that help the immune system fight off germs」，意即幫助免疫系統對抗病菌的蛋白質。選項 B 錯誤，抗體是防禦機制，而非病毒載體。選項 C 錯誤，文中將「疫苗」定義為預防疾病的藥物，而非抗體。選項 D 錯誤，抗體與身體疼痛無直接關聯，疼痛是感染後的症狀。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the dengue situation in Florida?

options.A: Florida's health officials have successfully eradicated the dengue virus through aggressive spraying.
options.B: The dengue virus is becoming a more persistent and challenging public health issue in the U.S. due to local spread.
options.C: The primary cause of the current outbreak is the high volume of travelers arriving from Puerto Rico.
options.D: Scientists have developed a new, highly effective vaccine that will soon end the outbreak in Tampa.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文旨在探討佛州登革熱疫情的嚴重性，強調其歷史紀錄、病毒的複雜性以及氣候變遷下病毒在地傳播的趨勢，顯示這已成為美國公共衛生的新挑戰。選項 A 錯誤，疫情仍在持續中。選項 C 雖然提到旅遊是因素之一，但並非文章探討的唯一核心。選項 D 錯誤，文中反而強調因病毒複雜性，疫苗研發極為困難。
